newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BRITISH FIRM TO ADVISE BULGARIA'S BALKAN AIRLINE.
newsitem.headline: BRITISH FIRM TO ADVISE BULGARIA'S BALKAN AIRLINE.

text.p: British consultancy firm KPMG will help Bulgaria's troubled national carrier Balkan Airline to work out a programme aimed at stabilising its finances, a transport ministry spokeswoman said on Monday.

"Balkan's stabilisation programme will be worked out by experts from the transport ministry and the airline together with Britain's KPMG and is expected to be ready by October 30," Valja Luleva told Reuters.
She said the decision on the programme, which should cut the airline's losses within a year, had been taken by a meeting of the transport ministry's chiefs earlier on Monday.
Balkan increased its losses in the first half of 1996 by 510 million levs against the same period last year, Luleva said. She gave no further details about the airline's finances.
Monday's meeting recommended that the airline increase international cargo and charter flights, officials said.
The government has provided emergency financial aid to Balkan of 1.4 billion levs to help offset its huge losses.
Bulgaria began procedures to privatise the national carrier in 1992 but in January 1995 the Privatisation Agency suspended them, citing a lack of buyers.
